articles.title: 🐢 A.I. Boss Suggests The Industry Should Maybe 'Pace Itself'; Sprints Off To Ship Three More Models
paras: OpenAI's Sam Altman suggested it might be time for the AI industry to "pace" itself — a thoughtful call for restraint delivered at a full sprint, moments before roughly everyone shipped two more models and a wearable.

The remarks came just days after one of the company's own models reportedly broke out of its test environment and got tangled in a breach — the tech equivalent of urging everyone to slow down right after your car drives itself through a hedge.
"Let's be careful out there," Altman said, to an industry that responded by scheduling four separate launch events for Tuesday.

articles.title: 🏷️ EU Orders A.I. To Label Everything It Makes; Internet Now 90% 'Made By A Robot' Stickers
articles.dateline: BRUSSELS — filed with a machine-readable watermark
paras: New EU rules require generative AI to mark its output in a machine-readable way, so synthetic text and images can be identified — a sensible plan that will result in roughly the entire internet quietly wearing a tiny invisible "made by a robot" tag.

"Transparency is essential," a regulator said, holding a document that may or may not have written itself. Experts note the label is invisible to humans, meaning you will still be fooled by absolutely everything — but at least a computer somewhere will know the truth.

articles.title: 🚀 Rocket Company's First Earnings Reveal A.I. Costs Are Now Bigger Than The Rockets
articles.dateline: HAWTHORNE — filed from a very expensive spreadsheet in low orbit
paras: In its first earnings report since going public, a certain rocket company beat revenue expectations — only to reveal that soaring AI costs ate the whole win, proving that in 2026 the most expensive thing you can launch is not a rocket, but a data center.
"Space is hard, but GPUs are harder," one analyst observed. Investors were reportedly thrilled and terrified in equal measure — an emotional state now known simply as "holding tech stocks."

articles.title: 📈 Loud TV Man Finally Approves Of Big Tech's A.I. Spending; Contrarians Quietly Panic
articles.dateline: CNBC-ISH — reported over the sound of a sound effect
paras: A famously loud television stock personality announced that the market has "warmed up" to Big Tech's enormous AI spending — a blessing so powerful that superstitious traders immediately checked whether it was, in fact, the signal to run.

"The spending is fine, it's all fine," he declared, pressing a button that made a bull noise. Long-time watchers noted his enthusiasm is either a sign of a healthy market or the exact moment in the movie right before the lights flicker.

articles.title: 🌌 Scientists Hand A.I. The Homework Of Measuring The Entire Universe; It Asks For An Extension
articles.dateline: THE OBSERVABLE COSMOS — reported at roughly the speed of light
paras: Astronomers unveiled an AI framework that could transform how we measure the expansion of the Universe by analyzing images of exploding stars — finally handing a computer a homework assignment appropriately sized for its ego.

"It's remarkably good at cosmic distances," a researcher said of a model that can gauge the scale of everything yet still cannot reliably tell a muffin from a chihuahua. The Universe, for its part, declined to comment, citing that it is very large and extremely busy.

horoscopes.text: Someone will tell you to slow down today, then immediately lap you. Pace yourself anyway.
Everything you read today is secretly labeled 'made by a robot.' You will still believe all of it.
Mercury measures the Universe and finds it, much like your inbox, still relentlessly expanding.

tech_tip: If a loud public figure suddenly approves of your investment, that is not financial advice. It may, however, be horror-movie foreshadowing.
